_readme: The road between the village and the town: walk south out of the village, arrive in the
It asserts which MAP the player is in rather than which tile. A tile assertion would be
pinned to how far a held key carried them after the transition - which is a fact about
the test's timing, not about warping.
The round trip is the point. A one-way test would pass with a warp that fires on every
frame the player stands on it - which, with a door at each end, bounces them between two
maps forever and looks like a freeze.
Every leg is held until a WALL stops it, so nothing here depends on counting tiles: the
north wall, then the east wall, then the road in the south-east corner.

steps.text: the title opens the game now. A --qa-script run points saves at user://qa_saves and empties it at boot, so there is never anything to Continue - and the cursor opens on the row a press will actually do something with, which is New game. Rows: Continue, New game. One press starts the run.
the warden opens the game now - hear her out before anything else
north wall, then east wall: two walls to stand on a known column
and south down that column, onto the road out of the village
standing still must NOT send us straight back
and north again through the town's own gate
and the village has not sent us straight back either
